L01.smt: (define-fun spec ((amount Int) (max_rate Int)) Bool (and (>= amount 0) (<= amount max_rate)))

L02.smt: (define-fun spec ((n Int) (max_rate Int)) Bool (<= n max_rate))
L02.ambiguity: yes: the slash in max_rate / time_period can be read as per (max_rate acquisitions per period) or as arithmetic division; read as per, so n <= max_rate within one period

L03.smt: (define-fun spec ((limit Int) (used Int) (cost Int)) Bool (<= (+ used cost) limit))
L03.ambiguity: yes: unclear whether the check accounts for prior consumption (used + cost <= limit) or compares cost alone against the limit (cost <= limit); chose used + cost <= limit, with exactly reaching the limit not counting as exceeding

L04.smt: (define-fun spec ((requested Int) (available Int)) Bool (<= requested available))

L05.smt: (define-fun spec ((k Int) (calls Int)) Bool (<= k calls))

L07.smt: (define-fun spec ((weight Int) (limit Int)) Bool (> weight limit))

L08.smt: (define-fun spec ((n Int) (limit Int)) Bool (<= n limit))

L09.smt: (define-fun spec ((existing Int) (amount Int) (limit Int)) Bool (<= (+ existing amount) limit))
L09.ambiguity: yes: unclear whether the weighted count compared to the limit is the count before this call (existing <= limit) or after adding the requested amount (existing + amount <= limit); chose the post-acquisition count, since the pre-acquisition reading lets a single call overshoot the limit

L10.smt: (define-fun spec ((n Int) (capacity Int)) Bool (<= n capacity))
